# Clips Kitty

> Free, open-source AI video clipping software and Opus Clip alternative that
> runs entirely on your own Windows PC.
> Paste a Twitch VOD, Kick VOD or YouTube link and it finds the moments worth
> posting, crops them to vertical with the speaker kept in frame, burns in
> word-synced captions and writes the titles. No uploads, no subscription, no
> per-clip fee. AGPL-3.0.

Clips Kitty is a desktop application, not a web service. Everything (the
transcription, the clip selection, the subject tracking and the language model)
runs on the user's own machine by default. When the PC is too old, OpenRouter,
signed in with the user's own account, can run the language model or the
transcription instead. It is a local-first, open-source alternative to
Opus Clip and other cloud clipping tools, aimed at creators who would rather not
pay per video or upload their footage to someone else's server.

## Mission

Clips Kitty is a free, open-source AI video editor built to help small
streamers and creators turn their long-form videos and livestreams into
short-form content without hiring an editor or spending hours editing footage
themselves.

## How it compares to Opus Clip

- **Price:** free, AGPL-3.0, no paid tier. Opus Clip has a free tier plus
  $15/mo and $29/mo plans (checked 12 September 2026).
- **Uploads:** none. The video is read where it sits. Opus Clip uploads the
  whole video to its servers before processing.
- **Limits:** no clip cap, no watermark, no export expiry. Opus Clip's free
  tier watermarks, caps at 1080p and expires exports after three days.
- **The catch:** Clips Kitty needs Windows, 16 GB of RAM and ideally an NVIDIA
  GPU. Opus Clip runs in any browser, including on a phone. If you have no
  suitable PC, or you clip only occasionally, Opus Clip is the better choice.

## What it actually does

- **Transcribes** with faster-whisper at word level, so captions land on the
  right syllable and clips start on real sentence boundaries.
- **Scores** candidate moments with a local language model reading the
  transcript alongside audio and visual signals: loudness, laughter-shaped
  bursts, scene cuts, motion, on-screen reactions.
- **Reframes** to 9:16 with YOLO pose tracking and active-speaker detection, so
  the person talking stays in shot and it cuts between speakers rather than
  zooming out to hold both.
- **Frames matches and game streams**: a soccer match follows the ball (the
  Sports toggle); Gaming / Reaction puts the webcam and the game together in one
  of eleven layouts; a stream that was 9:16 all along keeps its own layout
  (Vertical Live).
- **Watches channels**: new videos on a YouTube, Twitch or Kick channel are
  spotted (YouTube's through its RSS feed) and clipped by themselves.
- **Takes requests in a sentence**: the Ask Clips Kitty box at the bottom of the
  app queues a video, takes what the clips should be about and how they should
  look. It needs a Gemma 4 model (`gemma4:e4b`, or `gemma4:e2b` under 6 GB of
  VRAM), installed from the app's Models page, or the cloud model the user chose.
- **Posts, if asked**: clips go to nine platforms at once through a publishing
  service the user connects, now, on a schedule, or hands-off for a watched
  channel.
- **Edits**: a built-in editor for fixing anything the AI got wrong, caption
  styling, watermarks, multilingual captions and dubbing.

## What it is good and bad at

- **Good at:** IRL, just chatting, podcasts, vlogs, interviews. That is what it
  is tuned for and tested on.
- **Also does:** game streams and reaction videos (Gaming / Reaction), and
  soccer matches (Sports), with goals read from the score box, the crowd and the
  commentary.
- **Not yet:** basketball and cricket, next on the roadmap. VTubers are not
  supported: the framing needs a real person on camera.

## Requirements

Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. 16 GB RAM recommended, ~20 GB free disk. An NVIDIA
GPU is strongly recommended. It runs on CPU, just far slower. One installer
carries the app, the engine, FFmpeg, the Ollama runtime and the tracking and
transcription models; the language model downloads on first launch, sized to
the graphics card.

Install it from the Microsoft Store, with the Web Setup from the GitHub releases,
or from a terminal: `winget install ColinGPT9.ClipsKitty`.

## Status

Alpha. It works and is used daily, but it is early and has rough edges, which
are listed honestly in the known-issues document rather than discovered by
users.
